units.reason: Given the cited Liu–Wei KP-I lump nondegeneracy and standard fixed-point/implicit-function theorems, the new proof still constructs an inverse for a singularly perturbed coupled phase/amplitude operator uniformly as the transonic parameter tends to zero. It develops anisotropic Fourier-kernel bounds near the origin and at infinity, weighted convolution estimates with logarithmic losses, a KP-I limit contradiction argument removing the symmetric kernel, and large-disk adjoint/Fredholm solvability followed by passage to the plane. Source-term compatibility and nonlinear weighted estimates close a quantitative contraction and yield the C1 travelling-wave branch with O(epsilon^2|log epsilon|^2) convergence and the author energy–momentum conclusions. This is one nonroutine H3 singular-PDE construction, beyond merely applying the given lump nondegeneracy or Banach fixed-point theorem. The six legacy estimates and Euler–Korteweg adaptation share that proof core and are not additional independent problems.
